purpose: contract-matched ingest — store lanes (gigi lanes: vs_stores_embedded --batch-rows)

protocol.rows_source: data.csv parsed pre-window (except duckdb one-ack: read_csv in-clock)

environment.note: single Windows laptop, serial runs, nothing else running (operator-attested)

sqlite.mechanism: one BEGIN + executemany + COMMIT (round-1 cell, re-timed)

duckdb.mechanism: INSERT INTO txns SELECT FROM read_csv(...) — round-1 shape, CSV parse inside the clock (disclosed)

sqlite.mechanism: BEGIN + executemany(1000) + COMMIT per chunk — 100 transactions, journal defaults

duckdb.mechanism: BEGIN + executemany(1000) + COMMIT per chunk — 100 transactions, row-wise prepared statements

disclosures: CONTRACT MATCHING (round-4 clause 1): rounds 1-3 timed gigi under a 100-durability-ack contract against sqlite under a 1-ack contract. This file carries both matched pairs for the stores; the two gigi lanes come from the vs_stores_embedded binary (--batch-rows 100000 for one-ack; default 1000 for many-ack) and are reported side by side with these, never mixed across contracts.

MANY-ACK 'ack' definitions per system, honestly different in kind: sqlite COMMIT under journal_mode=delete + synchronous=full (fsync-backed rollback-journal commit per chunk); duckdb COMMIT of its WAL per chunk (durability semantics per duckdb defaults, version recorded); gigi batch_insert = WAL append + one fsync per call. Each system pays its own real per-ack cost; none is normalized to another's.

duckdb MANY-ACK uses row-wise prepared-statement executemany per chunk — NOT duckdb's idiomatic columnar bulk path. That is the honest shape of a 100-transaction contract from pre-parsed Python rows; the ONE-ACK lane shows duckdb's idiomatic path (read_csv, CSV parse inside the clock, as in round 1).

sqlite lanes reuse run_sqlite.py's DDL/INSERT/fresh_connection verbatim (txn_id PRIMARY KEY maintained during ingest, fresh file DB per rep, %TEMP% local disk outside the OneDrive-synced tree); duckdb lanes reuse run_duckdb.py's likewise.
All lanes in-process, strictly serial, GC handled uniformly by eval_common.warmup_plus_reps; this runner aborts if anything answers on 127.0.0.1:3143.
